picks.d: The world's largest free pop-up literary festival takes over the Mission for one glorious night — 250+ authors, 50+ events, nearly 5,000 fans spilling out of bookstores, bars, and galleries. Dog Eared Books, Sycamore, Martuni's and more become your personal literary playgrounds. Suggested donation $10–15, but your soul gets fed for free.

The Grammy-winning country-pop goddess plays Oakland Arena with opener Estevie — dreamy, introspective songwriting plus a lush stage production that'll genuinely give you chills. Yes it's technically across the bay, but this is a can't-miss arena moment. Grab your tickets now before they're gone.

picks.t: Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean — Asian Art Museum
picks.d: The largest ancient bronze ever found in Southeast Asia — a monumental Reclining Vishnu buried for centuries and rediscovered in 1936 — makes its final international tour stop right here in SF. This is a genuine once-in-a-lifetime cultural moment; the piece is unlikely to travel again after this. On view through January 25, 2027.

The Ferry Building transforms into a global dumpling wonderland with 25+ restaurants slinging dumplings from every corner of the world — plus live music, cooking demos, eating contests, and family activities. It's free to get in, so your only danger is ordering way too much. Highly recommended: go hungry.

One of SF's most beloved food traditions returns to the Wharf — free admission, legendary clam chowder, and that salty bay breeze you can't get anywhere else. It's touristy and we don't care, because warm bread bowls fix everything. Bring your appetite and your most elastic waistband.

Architects, engineers, designers, and elementary school kids team up to build jaw-dropping giant sand sculptures at Ocean Beach — and you get to watch it all unfold for free. It's weird, it's wonderful, it's very SF. The Pacific wind and the sheer ambition of these sand castles will humble you.

K Ishibashi brings his looped violins and orchestral indie-pop magic to the Fillmore for a full celebration of Sonderlust — a genuinely beautiful album turning 10. If you've never seen him layer live violin loops into something that sounds like a full orchestra, prepare to have your mind rearranged. One of the week's most special shows.

The comedian, author, and podcast host brings sharp observational wit and genuinely unhinged energy to Cobb's Comedy Club for four performances across the weekend. Multiple show times mean you can actually get a ticket — grab it. She's the kind of comic who makes you snort-laugh and then immediately feel seen.

picks.t: Illuminati Hotties at Great American Music Hall
picks.d: Sarah Tudzin's razor-sharp sardonic indie rock project takes over the GAMH with openers Buzzed Lightbeer, Satana Satana, and Swell Foop — it's a stacked Saturday bill. The Great American Music Hall is one of SF's most gorgeous rooms and Illuminati Hotties will absolutely shred it. This is the indie rock Saturday night of the week.

The beloved SNL veteran and Portlandia co-creator brings his musician-comedy hybrid show to the Castro Theatre for two nights — it's exactly as delightfully weird as it sounds. The Castro is one of the most iconic venues in the country, which makes even the seats feel like an event. Rare mid-week treat.

Adults-only Halloween night at the Exploratorium with themed exhibits, a cow eye dissection (yes, really), costume contest, and dancing to cumbia, darkwave, and post-punk with Los Goths Co. It's spooky, it's sciency, it's SO San Francisco. Reservations required — grab tickets before they sell out.

picks.t: Lower Polk Live! Free Street Festival
picks.d: Polk Street shuts down for a free neighborhood block party with live music, DJs, art, and local makers between Bush and Sutter — the perfect way to kick off your Friday before a show. It's low-key, it's community-driven, and it costs absolutely nothing. Just show up.

picks.t: Aquabats w/ Mariachi El Bronx — Regency Ballroom
picks.d: Legendary ska-punk superheroes in full costume, Mariachi El Bronx bringing their mariachi-punk hybrid, and Mrs. Magician — all on one bill at the beautiful Regency Ballroom. Whether you're bringing kids or just your inner kid, this is a genuinely joyful Friday night. One of the most fun shows of the week, no contest.

ongoing.t: Peter Pan Goes Wrong — SF Playhouse
ongoing.d: A play about a play catastrophically falling apart, running through Nov 28 — slapstick chaos at its most theatrical.
A breathtaking circus love letter to SF with acrobatics, shadow art, and juggling running nightly in North Beach.

ongoing.t: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
ongoing.d: BTS's RM curates a floor at SFMOMA featuring Korean artworks many Americans have never seen before.
The 17th annual festival runs Oct 23–Nov 8 at Lucasfilm Premier Theater and online — opens with Nureyev.

new.name: Shinka
new.d: Jean-Georges alum Fumio Yonezawa's debut SF restaurant inside The Jay Hotel — chawanmushi, miso cod, shio koji duck wellington, omakase or à la carte.

new.name: Lucania
new.d: From the A16 team, the revived Ferry Building flagship focuses on southern Italy — little fish, marinated anchovies, sardines, mussels, fresh pasta, and a killer dog-friendly patio.

new.name: 15 Romolo
new.d: The 115-year-old pseudo-speakeasy just reopened after a two-year renovation — Pimm's cups, sherry, and tapas in a refreshed bohemian interior.

new.name: Bayview Oyster Bar
new.d: New Orleans-style raw bar from the chef behind Auntie April's — grilled and raw oysters, clam chowder, Dungeness crab with garlic noodles in a Bayview neighborhood gem.

new.name: Hi NRG
new.d: The beloved espresso spot relaunched on Geary with expanded pastries, sandwiches, ice cream sundaes, and wine at night — neighborhood must.

new.name: Ah Ma's Kitchen
new.d: Cantonese flavors and Hong Kong vibes on Clement Street — a Yelp Best New Restaurant of 2026 that's already packed every night.

classic.name: City View Restaurant
classic.d: Longtime Chinatown favorite for weekend dim sum — cart service, crispy taro dumplings, and a dining room that fills up fast.

classic.name: Bix
classic.d: A Gold Rush-era supper club vibe in an old alley off Jackson — martinis, live jazz, and the kind of duck confit that haunts you.

classic.name: La Taqueria
classic.d: James Beard Award-winning carnitas burritos and tacos on Mission Street — no rice, no apologies, just the best in the city.

classic.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
classic.d: Multiple world champion pizza maker Tony Gemignani's flagship — the different ovens for different regional styles is genuinely nerdy and genuinely delicious.

classic.name: Scoma's
classic.d: Pier 47 institution since 1965 — fresh-off-the-boat Dungeness crab, cioppino, and a bay view that never gets old.

classic.name: Mensho Tokyo
classic.d: Chef Toru Abe's SF outpost serves some of the most complex, inventive ramen in the country — be ready to wait in line and not regret it.

bars.name: 15 Romolo
bars.d: Freshly renovated speakeasy-ish gem down a North Beach alley — sherry, Pimm's, and a vibe that's too fancy to be a dive and too cool to be anything else.

bars.name: Bar Part Time
bars.d: SF's danciest natural wine bar with low-intervention pours and a crowd that actually dances — the partners are opening a new nightclub soon so soak this in.

bars.name: Noc Noc
bars.d: One of SF's great weird dives — art-covered walls, cheap drinks, and an eclectic crowd that doesn't take itself too seriously.

bars.name: Brass Tacks
bars.d: Elevated cocktails in a small, intimate Hayes Valley room — thoughtful menu, zero pretension, ideal for a proper date night drink.

bars.name: Bourbon & Branch
bars.d: The legendary SF speakeasy with password entry, library-quiet rules, and exceptional whiskey and cocktails — book a reservation or you're not getting in.

bars.name: The Thirsty Bear
bars.d: Organic craft beer brewed on-site with Spanish tapas in a cavernous SoMa space — great for Warriors game nights this week.

bars.name: Charmaine's at Proper Hotel
bars.d: The rooftop perch above Union Square with sweeping city views, good natural wine, and a crowd that skews stylish but not insufferable.

bars.name: Halcyon SF
bars.d: SF's beloved late-night techno institution on 11th Street — Victor Ruiz plays Friday night and the Funktion-One system will rearrange your organs in the best way.

sports.note: Great early-season energy at Chase Center — grab a seat and soak in the home opener vibes.
This could be a series-clinching game for SF's own Valkyries — genuinely historic if they close it out at home.

concerts.d: Grammy-winning country-pop artist at Oakland Arena with opener Estevie — dreamy, lush production and some of the best songwriting in the game right now. Yes, it's Oakland, but the BART ride is worth it. One of the biggest shows of the week.

K Ishibashi celebrates the 10th anniversary of his beloved Sonderlust album at the Fillmore — live looped violin, orchestral pop arrangements, and a room that was literally built for this kind of show. If you only see one show this week, make it this one or the next one.

Sarah Tudzin's sardonic, sharp, endlessly fun indie rock project with a stacked supporting bill — Buzzed Lightbeer, Satana Satana, and Swell Foop. The Great American Music Hall is a gorgeous room and this is the indie rock Saturday night you've been waiting for.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check GAMH

concerts.d: The country-rap crossover phenomenon brings his Americana-meets-hip-hop sound to The Masonic — massive chart success means this room will be electric. If you've been sleeping on Shaboozey, this is your wake-up call.

concerts.w: Tue Oct 28 SOLD OUT · Wed Oct 29 · 8 PM
concerts.d: Chicago's beloved slowcore/shoegaze band sold out Tuesday at the Fillmore — a true testament to their devoted following. Wednesday's second night is your chance; grab it now before it follows suit. Emotionally heavy, lush guitar work in one of SF's best rooms.

concerts.t: The Aquabats w/ Mariachi El Bronx
concerts.d: Costumed ska-punk superheroes plus the mariachi-punk hybrid brilliance of Mariachi El Bronx at the beautiful Regency Ballroom — one of the most purely fun shows on the calendar this week. Bring your kids or just your most enthusiastic self.

concerts.t: Inner Wave w/ Heathers, The Fazes, Christina's Trip
concerts.d: LA-based psychedelic surf-pop with a dreamy, lush sound and a stacked supporting lineup — the Great American Music Hall on a Monday night has its own special energy. A great way to ease into the week.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check GAMH

concerts.t: Pixel Grip w/ Dark Chisme, Grizz, Blood Rave
concerts.d: Chicago industrial dance trio with a dark synth-heavy sound paired with a perfectly Halloween-adjacent supporting lineup — Blood Rave alone is a name that sells a Wednesday night. Mid-week dark dance energy at its finest.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check GAMH

concerts.t: Wand w/ Cole Berliner & The Grizzled Mighty
concerts.d: Genre-fluid LA rockers Wand bring their krautrock-to-folk-to-noise-rock shapeshifting sound to the GAMH — a perfect alternative if you couldn't snag Slow Pulp tickets on the same night. Two great shows, one great decision.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check GAMH

concerts.t: Julia Wolf (w/ Bee Blackwell) — Deep End World Tour
concerts.d: Emotionally raw indie-pop songwriter Julia Wolf at the grand old Warfield with opener Bee Blackwell — hook-driven, confessional, and the kind of show that sticks with you. A fantastic Friday option if arena shows aren't your thing.

concertsOngoing.d: Sat Oct 25 at Cow Palace — one of the weekend's biggest electronic live music draws, presented by Another Planet.

concertsOngoing.t: Dermot Kennedy — Weight of the Woods Tour
concertsOngoing.d: Sat Oct 25 at Bill Graham Civic Auditorium — the Irish singer-songwriter plays SF's iconic venue.
Fri Oct 24 at The Fillmore — dark atmospheric underground hip-hop and trap for the devoted.
Fri Oct 24 at Herbst Theatre — steampunk theatrical pop with intricate vocal harmonies in a gorgeous room.

singles.t: Lit Crawl SF — Best Accidental Date Night in the City
singles.d: Wander the Mission together through 50+ events at bars, bookstores, and galleries — it's effortlessly romantic, endlessly interesting, and free. You'll always have something to talk about because something is always happening. Suggested donation $10–15 if you want to support the cause.

singles.t: FALL for Someone SF Speed Dating (Ages 25–45)
singles.d: Classic speed dating at ERIA Marina in the Marina District — check-in at 6:45, mingling before 7:15, then you're off to the races meeting new people every 5–7 minutes. It's dog-friendly, has a dedicated host, and street parking is available. Low pressure, high potential.

Brazilian techno powerhouse Victor Ruiz at one of SF's best late-night rooms — the Funktion-One system hits different and the crowd is always a good time. Show up a little early, introduce yourself to the person next to you, and just let the music do the work. 21+.

singles.t: Run Club SF — Thursday Speedwork at Kezar
singles.d: Kezar Stadium on a fall evening with a social running crew — beginner-friendly pace, genuinely fun group, and the kind of endorphin high that makes post-run hangouts inevitable. It's how a lot of SF friendships (and more) have started. Seasonal registration required.

singles.t: Ivy Lab Farewell Tour at Public Works
singles.d: The farewell tour of one of drum and bass's most beloved acts, with Mr. Carmack b2b Great Dane and DJ Dials — a genuinely historic night in a community-minded club with an incredible sound system. Tickets sold out on Eventbrite so check TickPick or SeatGeek. 21+.

singles.t: Psyched! Fest — Latin Electronic Takeover at Monarch
singles.d: Full-venue Latin electronic takeover at Monarch SF celebrating the Bay Area's Latin underground — Latincore, cumbia, baile funk, techno, perreo, and 2AT all the way from Bogotá for a special US stop. One of the most unique lineups of the week and a genuinely electric room.

singlesOngoing.t: Midnight Runners SF — Wednesday Night City Run
singlesOngoing.d: Wed Oct 29 at 6:30 PM — music, workout stops, and a club-like atmosphere through SF streets. Find meeting point on Heylo.
Coed 6v6 competitive volleyball Tuesdays in Potrero Hill and Thursdays in the Mission — great way to meet people mid-week.

date.title: Mission Literary Crawl Night
date.tagline: Stumble into something beautiful — no wallet required.

steps.title: Meet at Lit Crawl SF
steps.detail: Start at Dog Eared Books or Medicine for Nightmares on Valencia — pick a reading that sounds interesting and just walk in together. The energy is immediately warm and a little electric.

steps.title: Bounce between venues
steps.detail: Check the Lit Crawl schedule and hop to wherever sounds good — a bar reading, a gallery performance, a bookstore short story set. Let the night surprise you.

steps.title: Wind down with a drink
steps.detail: The Mission has no shortage of good bars — grab a natural wine at Bar Part Time or a beer at any number of spots on Valencia and debrief on your favorite moment of the night.

date.title: Dumpling Sunday + Kishi Bashi at the Fillmore
date.tagline: Feed your stomach, then your soul.

steps.title: SF World of Dumplings at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Arrive early at the Ferry Building for the World of Dumplings Festival — sample your way through 25+ restaurants and grab the ones that make you fight over the last bite.

steps.title: Walk the Embarcadero
steps.detail: Burn off some dumpling calories with a walk along the water — pop into the Ferry Building proper for a coffee or a browse through the shops.

steps.title: Dinner at Lucania
steps.detail: The newly opened southern Italian restaurant at the Ferry Building is right there — try the little fish section and share a pasta before the show.

steps.title: Kishi Bashi at the Fillmore
steps.detail: Head over to the Fillmore for the Sonderlust 10th Anniversary show — looped violins, orchestral beauty, and one of SF's most storied rooms. Grab a poster on the way out.

date.title: Chowder Fest Afternoon + Kacey Musgraves at Oakland Arena
date.tagline: A full day-into-night memory-maker across the bay.

steps.title: Fisherman's Wharf Chowder Fest
steps.detail: Start at the Wharf for the Chowder Fest — classic SF afternoon with bread bowls, bay breezes, and a crowd that's always in a good mood.

steps.title: Cocktails at Scoma's or the Wharf
steps.detail: Sit down for a proper drink at Scoma's bar with a bay view — a Dungeness crab appetizer doesn't hurt either.

steps.title: BART across the bay
steps.detail: Take BART from Powell or Civic Center to Oakland Coliseum station — quick, painless, no parking nightmare.

steps.title: Kacey Musgraves at Oakland Arena
steps.detail: Settle in for one of the best arena shows of the fall — dreamy, lush, emotionally resonant. Opener Estevie is worth arriving early for.

solo.title: Ocean Beach Saturday Morning
solo.tagline: Clear your head before the weekend gets loud.

steps.title: LEAP Sandcastle Classic at Ocean Beach
steps.detail: Walk down to Ocean Beach and watch teams of architects and engineers build enormous sand sculptures — it's completely free, genuinely impressive, and the kind of weird SF thing you'll tell people about.

steps.title: Fisherman's Wharf Chowder Fest
steps.detail: Head up to the Wharf for a bowl of chowder — free to get in, just pay for what you eat. Budget $10–15 for a solid lunch.

steps.title: Walk or bike the waterfront home
steps.detail: Take the scenic route back along the Embarcadero — stop at the Ferry Building, grab a coffee, and feel very pleased with yourself for having a perfect free Saturday.

solo.title: Cultural Deep Dive — Vishnu + SFMOMA
solo.tagline: Two world-class exhibitions, one excellent afternoon.

steps.title: Asian Art Museum — Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean
steps.detail: The largest ancient bronze ever found in Southeast Asia, on loan from Cambodia, opens this week. Go early to avoid crowds. Budget about 90 minutes and let yourself be genuinely amazed.

steps.title: Lunch at a Hayes Valley spot
steps.detail: Walk to Hayes Valley for lunch — grab something at one of the neighborhood's cafes and people-watch for a bit.

steps.title: SFMOMA — RM x Between You and Me
steps.detail: Head over to SFMOMA and spend time on Floor 7 with RM's curated collection of Korean artworks. Also check out the Raven Chacon commission opening this week. The museum is endlessly walkable.

steps.title: Cocktail at Brass Tacks
steps.detail: Finish the afternoon at Brass Tacks in Hayes Valley — thoughtful cocktails, zero pretension, perfect for sitting at the bar solo with no one bothering you.

solo.title: Omakase Solo Dinner at Shinka
solo.tagline: The most self-loving thing you'll do all month.

steps.title: Pre-dinner walk through FiDi
steps.detail: Arrive in the Financial District early and walk around — Battery Street has a different energy on weekend evenings when the suits are gone.

steps.title: Omakase at Shinka
steps.detail: Book a seat at the chef's counter at Shinka inside The Jay Hotel — Jean-Georges alum Fumio Yonezawa's Japanese-French tasting menu is a genuine debut worth catching early. Chawanmushi, miso cod, shio koji duck wellington. Take your time.

steps.title: Late drink at Bourbon & Branch
steps.detail: Walk or rideshare to the Tenderloin and get your password for Bourbon & Branch — settle in with an exceptional whiskey or cocktail and feel very adult and very fine about being alone.

birthday.title: Lit Crawl Birthday Bar Hop
birthday.tagline: The literary bar crawl no one knew they needed for their birthday.

steps.title: Meet at Lit Crawl SF in the Mission
steps.detail: Gather the crew at a Mission starting point for Lit Crawl — pick a fun-sounding reading or event to kick things off. The birthday person picks the first venue, obviously.

steps.title: Reading + bar rotation
steps.detail: Work your way through Lit Crawl venues that double as bars — Sycamore and Martuni's are great picks. Order drinks, catch snippets of readings, repeat.

steps.title: Dinner on Valencia
steps.detail: Land somewhere on Valencia Street for a proper birthday dinner — the Mission has every price point. Make a reservation in advance so you're not scrambling.

birthday.title: Chowder Fest Day + Illuminati Hotties Night
birthday.tagline: A perfect birthday arc: salty, silly, loud.

steps.title: Fisherman's Wharf Chowder Fest
steps.detail: Start the birthday celebration with a midday trip to the Chowder Fest — free admission, legendary chowder, great group energy. Make the birthday person eat a comically large bread bowl.

steps.title: Explore North Beach
steps.detail: Walk to North Beach for an afternoon aperitivo at 15 Romolo — the newly reopened speakeasy is a perfect birthday afternoon pitstop. Sherry cocktails, tapas, good vibes.

steps.title: Illuminati Hotties at Great American Music Hall
steps.detail: Head to the GAMH for Illuminati Hotties with the full crew — doors at 7, show at 7:30. Sarah Tudzin will absolutely deliver. The GAMH is one of SF's best rooms for a group.

steps.title: Dinner at Lucania
steps.detail: Pre-show dinner at the newly opened Lucania at the Ferry Building — southern Italian, excellent fish dishes, and a waterfront vibe that sets the right celebratory tone. Make a reservation.

steps.title: BART to Oakland
steps.detail: Take BART from Embarcadero to Oakland Coliseum — quick, easy, no parking stress. Arrive with time to grab drinks inside the arena.

steps.title: Kacey Musgraves at Oakland Arena
steps.detail: Settle into the arena for the full Kacey Musgraves experience — lush production, dreamy setlist, and the kind of show where everyone in your group ends the night saying it was the best one yet.

friends.title: Lower Polk Live then Lit Crawl
friends.tagline: Two free festivals, one legendary Friday.

steps.title: Lower Polk Live! Street Festival
steps.detail: Meet on Polk Street between Bush and Sutter for the free neighborhood block party — live music, DJs, art, local makers, and the kind of crowd that's just happy to be outside. Stay as long as you want.

steps.title: Grab dinner in the neighborhood
steps.detail: Walk up Polk Street for a cheap dinner — there are solid options at every price point and you're already there.

steps.title: Migrate to Lit Crawl in the Mission
steps.detail: Head over to the Mission for Lit Crawl SF — let the group split up, hit different events, and reconvene at a bar to compare notes. It's the most fun you can have for free on a Saturday night in SF.

friends.title: Dumplings + Exploratorium Creepatorium
friends.tagline: Eat around the world, then get spooked by science.

steps.title: World of Dumplings at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Start Sunday at the World of Dumplings Festival — assign everyone a different dumpling to report back on and then eat each other's findings. It's a group activity disguised as eating.

steps.title: Afternoon at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Browse the Ferry Building shops, grab a coffee, and wander the Embarcadero. Low-key decompression before the evening picks up.

steps.title: Exploratorium After Dark: Creepatorium
steps.detail: Head to Pier 15 for the adults-only Halloween Creepatorium — themed exhibits, cow eye dissection, costume contest, and dancing to darkwave and cumbia with Los Goths Co. 18+ and reservations required. Book ahead.

friends.title: Aquabats + Marc Rebillet Block Party Weekend
friends.tagline: The most chaotic, joyful weekend on the calendar.

steps.title: The Aquabats at Regency Ballroom
steps.detail: Start Friday night with the Aquabats — costumed ska-punk superheroes, Mariachi El Bronx, and a Regency Ballroom crowd that came to have the best time. Energy level: unhinged (in a great way).

steps.title: Marc Rebillet, Franc Moody & Chromeo Block Party at The Midway
steps.detail: Saturday afternoon into night at The Midway in Dogpatch — this daytime block party with three stacked acts is genuinely one of the best group hangs of the week. Tickets from $47.

steps.title: After-party or late night at 1015 Folsom
steps.detail: CID is at 1015 Folsom after the block party winds down — the legendary SoMa institution is the perfect capstone to a two-night friends weekend. Pace yourselves.

parents.title: Sandcastle Classic + Ferry Building Morning
parents.tagline: A perfect no-cost Saturday with the family.

steps.title: LEAP Sandcastle Classic at Ocean Beach
steps.detail: Watch teams of architects and elementary school kids build giant sand sculptures at Ocean Beach — it's free, fascinating, and kids absolutely love watching the construction unfold. Dress in layers.

steps.title: Fisherman's Wharf Chowder Fest
steps.detail: Head up to the Wharf for the Chowder Fest — free entry, legendary clam chowder, and a Fisherman's Wharf afternoon that the whole family can enjoy. Budget for food and drinks.

steps.title: Ferry Building browse
steps.detail: Walk the Embarcadero to the Ferry Building for a browse — pick up something for the week, grab a pastry, and let the kids stare at the bay for a while. Perfect low-key ending.

parents.title: Aquabats Family Show Night
parents.tagline: The one concert where bringing the kids makes you the cool parent.

steps.title: Early dinner in the neighborhood
steps.detail: Grab dinner near the Regency Ballroom before the show — the Tenderloin/Civic Center area has solid options, or bring snacks for the kids.

steps.title: The Aquabats at Regency Ballroom
steps.detail: The Aquabats are legitimately family-friendly — costumed superhero ska-punk with theatrical energy and Mariachi El Bronx and Mrs. Magician on the same bill. Kids will lose their minds. So will you.

steps.title: Ice cream on the way home
steps.detail: The Aquabats will have the kids wired — channel that energy into a post-show ice cream walk and let everyone relive their favorite moment of the night.

parents.title: Vishnu Exhibition + Shinka Dinner
parents.tagline: Culture, wonder, and a truly special meal.

steps.title: Asian Art Museum — Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean
steps.detail: The monumental Reclining Vishnu from Cambodia opens this week — a once-in-a-generation exhibition that's genuinely awe-inspiring for adults and older kids alike. Plan 90 minutes and read up on the history beforehand.

steps.title: Lunch in Hayes Valley
steps.detail: Walk to Hayes Valley for a proper lunch — the neighborhood has excellent options and a walkable, pleasant afternoon energy for families.

steps.title: SFMOMA — RM x Between You and Me
steps.detail: Head over to SFMOMA for the RM collection on Floor 7 — Korean artworks many Americans have never seen before, in a beautifully curated presentation. Older kids who know BTS will have a full moment.

steps.title: Dinner at Shinka
steps.detail: Book ahead at Shinka inside The Jay Hotel for a celebratory tasting menu dinner — the Japanese-French fusion is refined but not stuffy, and the chawanmushi alone is worth the reservation.
